question: Does the opposite relation of each W23 relation reach the event?
number: Among the 2585 EXACT samples of 2 seeds (2^26 samples; rows 22,23,25 cells dropped, prefix as printed): W23[0]!=W23[30]: printed 2585, opposite 0. W23[14]=W23[21]: printed 2585, opposite 0. W23[1]!=W23[31]: printed 1892, opposite 693 (26.8 percent). W23[16]=W23[25]: printed 2037, opposite 548 (21.2 percent). With the full cell conjunction and one relation flipped, cell hits are 0 for all four (base 1012). So two relations are implied by the event; for [1,31] and [16,25] the opposite relation reaches the event, inside the EXACT-outside-cells part (EXACT/cells 2.554) that is already counted.
notes: Universe cell sha256-38|r23|REL|Q4. No new gain: the event-looser-than-cells gain (+1.35 bit) is the known S38-EX-c38; the W23 exact set was already scanned and was not redone. Method: variant chi38 file per alternative (work/chi/*.txt, generated by work/gen.py from chi/chi38.txt; every other line unchanged), traillab window --rows 22 37 --event out --no-elist --autolist --np 4096 --mt 8192 --threads 3, seeds 9301,9302 (and 9303,9304 where an alternative stayed alive); unmodified chi38 reproduces atlas_runs38/H-drops/out/base.txt bit for bit on seeds 9301,9302 (work/out/_regression_base.txt: EXACT 1320/1265, prefix -84.995/-85.055). 'dead' = the SMC stage accepted 0 of 1,048,576 proposals on each seed. Window/prefix model only (no full-path check).
